rationale: All four lenses and the standards audit ran with parseable output; six candidates were dismissed after verifying reachability against source (docstring fix confirmed correct, GoogleDoc client construction confirmed handled by the base class __init__, PROVIDER context confirmed unrelated to the retrieval backend since IndexInfo is Postgres-backed, exception-type variance confirmed to match each layer's own existing convention, main.py's router-vs-service-layer gating split confirmed intentional, and the code-index error wording is cosmetic). Six findings survive, one critical: tool_execution_service.py's direct-invoke path bypasses the retrieval gate the rest of the diff applies (CR-004), plus an ungated re-index trigger actor (CR-006), an unvalidated RETRIEVAL_BACKEND value (CR-001), a standards-flagged untyped helper parameter (CR-002), no regression test for main.py's disabled-branch conditionals (CR-003), and an unconfirmed Codebase Tools catalogue entry whose external package contents could not be fully verified within budget, capped at major (CR-005). No decision_needed items and nothing deferred.

findings.title: RETRIEVAL_BACKEND lacks value validation
findings.problem: RETRIEVAL_BACKEND is declared as a plain str (default "elasticsearch") with no Literal/enum constraint; retrieval_available() only special-cases the exact string "none".
findings.impact: A typo, casing variant ("None"/"NONE"), stray whitespace, or an unimplemented future value (e.g. the inline-commented "pgvector") silently evaluates as available, leaving KB/datasource/code-indexing features turned on against a backend that isn't actually configured -- the opposite of AC29's intent.
findings.recommendation: Constrain the field, e.g. RETRIEVAL_BACKEND: Literal["elasticsearch", "none"] = "elasticsearch", or add a field_validator that normalizes/rejects unrecognized values.

findings.title: retrieval_available() cfg parameter untyped
findings.problem: def retrieval_available(cfg) -> bool leaves the cfg parameter without a type annotation, while the return type is annotated and every other new function/site in this diff is fully typed.
findings.impact: Violates the project's documented code-quality standard requiring explicit parameter and return types on new public functions.
findings.recommendation: Annotate the parameter: def retrieval_available(cfg: Config) -> bool:

findings.title: No regression test for RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=none boot branches
findings.problem: Both module-scope conditionals gating the ES-backed StateImportService().import_indexes() call (main.py:894-895) and the index.router registration (main.py:902-903) have no test exercising the RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=none branch; plan.md explicitly notes no black-box router-absence test is planned, and the two existing main.py-importing tests re-run only under the default (elasticsearch) config.
findings.impact: If either condition were ever inverted or checked the wrong flag, the app would either crash on boot (import_indexes attempting an ES bulk import with no backend) or keep leaking /v1/index/* endpoints (present-and-failing, the outcome AC29 forbids) -- and no test in the suite would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that imports codemie.rest_api.main with RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=none (patch + reload or subprocess import) and asserts both that StateImportService.import_indexes is never called and that no /v1/index/* route is present on app.routes.

findings.title: Direct tool invocation bypasses retrieval gating
findings.problem: ToolExecutionService._get_context_tools builds SearchKBTool/CodeToolkit tools for KNOWLEDGE_BASE/CODE context (lines 311-321) without checking retrieval_available(config), unlike the sibling ToolkitService.add_context_tools which this diff makes raise ToolException for the same two context types.
findings.impact: POST /v1/tools/{tool_name}/invoke -> invoke_tool_with_system_integration -> _get_context_tools is reachable via tool.router, which is registered unconditionally (main.py:928). With RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=none, a client can still hit this path and reach Elasticsearch-backed tool construction, failing deep inside instead of getting the clean disabled-feature error the rest of the diff establishes -- present-and-failing rather than absent, contradicting AC29.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same `if context.context_type in (ContextType.KNOWLEDGE_BASE, ContextType.CODE) and not retrieval_available(config): raise ...` guard inside _get_context_tools (or its caller) before dispatching to KB/code tool construction.

findings.title: Codebase Tools catalogue entry not fully hidden
findings.problem: When retrieval is unavailable, get_tools_info() skips _merge_code_toolkit entirely (line 77-78), but the autodiscovered toolkits list from toolkit_provider.get_available_toolkits_info() may already contain a CODEBASE_TOOLS entry independent of the ES-backed merge.
findings.impact: The tool catalogue could still list a 'Codebase Tools' toolkit when retrieval is disabled, missing only the merged backend tools -- contradicting the hide-features goal if that entry has no non-retrieval tools of its own. Reachability inside the external codemie_tools package could not be fully confirmed within budget; graded uncertain and capped at major.
findings.recommendation: Verify what toolkit_provider.get_available_toolkits_info() registers under CODEBASE_TOOLS; if it depends on the ES-backed merge to be non-empty/meaningful, filter it out explicitly when retrieval is unavailable, mirroring the KB toolkit's gating.

findings.title: Datasource re-index trigger actor not gated
findings.problem: The scheduled/triggered Google Doc re-index actor instantiates GoogleDocDatasourceProcessor and runs .reprocess/.index unconditionally; no retrieval_available(config) guard exists anywhere in this file, unlike the other ES-backed call sites this diff gates.
findings.impact: A cron-scheduled or triggered re-index for a pre-existing datasource fires even when RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=none, instantiating an ES-backed processor (the base class __init__ still constructs an ElasticSearchClient) and attempting indexing against a disabled backend instead of failing cleanly -- present-and-failing rather than absent, the outcome AC29 forbids.
findings.recommendation: Add the same `if not retrieval_available(config): logger.warning(...); return` guard used at other gated call sites, before constructing GoogleDocDatasourceProcessor.
